## The World’s Biggest Airports in 2025
Below are the top 13 biggest airports, in countries including Saudi Arabia, Malaysia, and the USA.
### 1. King Fahd International Airport (DMM)
​​Step into King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia and you’re stepping into a record-breaker! Covering a staggering 780 square kilometers (about 301 square miles), King Fahd International Airport is the biggest airport in the world. It’s so big, it eclipses several countries in size. Imagine an airport larger than Malta, Vatican City, and even neighboring Bahrain!
The terminal, covering 327,000 square meters, is a bustling hub for over 10 million travelers each year. Its two 4,000-meter runways accommodate the biggest birds in the sky. But what really makes King Fahd International stand out are its connections. The most popular routes include flights to Dubai, Cairo, and Istanbul.
Dammam, the airport’s home, is a hidden gem in Saudi Arabia. It’s a city where modernity meets tradition, offering stunning coastlines, cultural landmarks, and a peek into the Kingdom’s vibrant heart. It’s a city I definitely recommend visiting!
The world’s largest airport is King Fahd International Airport.
### 2. King Khalid International Airport (RUH)
Let me take you to King Khalid International Airport, a true giant in Riyadh. With an area of 225 square kilometers (about 87 square miles), it’s the second-largest airport in the world after King Fahd International. It’s not just its size that’s impressive, though.
This airport is a hive of activity, serving as the primary gateway to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia’s bustling capital. With five terminals and constant flights, it’s always alive with travelers. The most popular routes include Dubai, Jeddah, and Cairo.
Riyadh itself is a must-visit. It’s a city where skyscrapers touch the sky and ancient traditions are still cherished. From shopping in luxurious malls to exploring historical sites, Riyadh has it all. Trust me, whether you’re just passing through or staying in Riyadh, King Khalid International is your gateway to an adventure in this dynamic city.
Let me show you around RUH, one of Riyadh’s great giants. | Image Credit: King Khalid International Airport
### 3. Denver International Airport (DEN)
Welcome to Denver International Airport, the biggest airport in the US! Spanning a massive 53 square miles, it’s not just big, it’s colossal. That’s larger than the cities of Boston, Miami, or San Francisco. Imagine an airport where the runways and terminals stretch as far as the eye can see.
Denver International is a bustling hub, connecting travelers to destinations far and wide. If you’re heading to a domestic hotspot or an international locale, this airport is your gateway.
And let’s talk about Denver! This city is a treasure trove of experiences. Located at the foot of the Rocky Mountains, it offers a blend of urban sophistication and outdoor adventure. From exploring the vibrant arts scene to hiking in breathtaking landscapes, there’s no shortage of things to do in Denver.

If you’re just passing through or here to explore, Denver International Airport is your starting point for a Colorado adventure.
Envision DEN with endless runways and terminals extending to the horizon.
### 4. Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KUL)
Kuala Lumpur International Airport, or KUL, is a marvel in Malaysia. As the biggest airport in Asia, KUL is a massive 100-square-kilometer (39-square-mile) world of its own. That’s more than eight times the size of London Heathrow!
Transferring between these terminals is a breeze, thanks to a free shuttle bus service. Whether you’re catching a long-haul flight or hopping around Asia, KUL connects you seamlessly.
Kuala Lumpur is one of my favorite cities in the world. From towering skyscrapers to lush green parks, the city is a blend of modernity and tradition. There’s so much to explore, from street food adventures to cultural landmarks. It’s the getaway to the most beautiful places in Malaysia.
KUL connects you easily whether you’re traveling across Asia or on a long-haul journey.
### 5. Istanbul Airport (IST)
Next up on our list of the world’s largest airports is Istanbul Airport (IST), covering 29.5 square miles. This giant is making waves as a future contender for the title of the world’s busiest airport. With its grand opening in 2019, IST is set to serve a staggering 200 million passengers yearly by 2025. Nestled 22 miles from Istanbul, it’s got the space and ambition to expand massively.
Credit: en.wikipedia.org
IST is a gateway to the enchanting city of Istanbul. The airport’s modern design, including its iconic tulip-shaped tower, mirrors the city’s blend of tradition and innovation. Inside, you’re treated to Turkish Airlines’ luxurious lounges and a variety of dining options.
Now, if you’re heading into Istanbul, get ready for a city that’s a feast for the senses. From the historic grandeur of the Hagia Sophia to the vibrant colors and scents of the Grand Bazaar, Istanbul is a city that never fails to amaze. My advice? Take a Bosphorus cruise. It’s the best way to see the city from a different perspective.
With six runways in the works, IST is evolving into a global aviation powerhouse. Whether you’re passing through or diving into Istanbul’s wonders, this airport is your starting point for an adventure!
INSIDER TIP: Again, I highly recommend signing up for Going.com (Scott’s Cheap Flights) to find the best deals. Last year, I got an email alert on a $429 roundtrip fare from Boston to Istanbul with Turkish Airlines. The premium version is 100% worth the money, but I would at least sign up for the free version to save big on airfare this year.

Istanbul’s allure may be reached through IST.
### 6. Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW)
The second-largest airport in the US is Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW), a true titan at 26 square miles. That’s bigger than the island of Manhattan, and it even has its own zip code! With five terminals and 168 gates, DFW is a powerhouse in the aviation world.
Credit: @dfwairport on Instagram
American Airlines calls DFW home, and it’s easy to see why. This airport is a leader in sustainability, aiming for net-zero emissions by 2030 with a zero-carbon electrical plant. Seven runways here manage over 73 million passengers a year. Inside, you’ve got a feast of food choices, a walking path, and even a yoga studio to unwind.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) about the World’s Biggest Airports
Are you still curious about which airport is the biggest in the world? Here are some popular questions (and answers) I get that will help answer your queries.
### Is Heathrow one of the biggest airports in the world?
Heathrow Airport, while one of the busiest in terms of passenger traffic, isn’t one of the largest when it comes to physical size. It’s known more for its high volume of international passengers.
### What is the largest airport in the world by size?
King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, holds the title for the largest airport in the world by size. It covers a staggering 780 square kilometers (about 301 square miles).
### Which airport is the biggest in Europe?
In terms of passenger traffic, London Heathrow Airport is the biggest airport in Europe. However, if we’re talking about physical size, Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport is one of the largest, covering about 32.38 square kilometers (12.5 square miles).
It’s more than simply an airport; it’s a vast area the size of several cities.
### What airport has the most runways?
Chicago O’Hare International Airport has the most runways of any airport in the world, with a total of 8 runways.
### What airport has the most flights per day?
Before the pandemic, Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport in the USA had the most flights per day. It’s renowned for being one of the busiest airports in terms of both passenger traffic and flight operations.
